blogPost.title: Small Bathroom Ideas: Design, Layout, and Remodel Tips for Small Spaces
blogPost.content:
The small bathroom remodel ideas that work best free up floor space and open sightlines. New finishes alone won't make a 40-square-foot room feel bigger.

A small bathroom remodel averages $6,500 in 2026, and most projects land between $1,500 and $15,000, according to Angi's cost data. Where you fall in that range depends mostly on one decision: whether the toilet, sink and shower stay where they are. Moving them adds about $5,000.

If you only do a few things, do these. Mount the vanity on the wall so the floor shows underneath. Swap the shower curtain for clear glass. Hang one large mirror and add light at face height. Use large-format tile in a light color. Together they make the same footprint feel larger without moving a wall.

The most popular change this year is a bigger shower. Just under half of renovating homeowners enlarged theirs, according to the 2026 U.S. Houzz Bathroom Trends Study.

Below are 27 small bathroom remodel ideas sorted into three budget levels. Each one explains what you gain, what it costs where pricing is available, and whether it's a job you can do yourself. The budget levels are estimates, so get local quotes before you commit.

Measure first: what fits in a small bathroom

Measure before you choose a single tile. Building codes set a minimum clear space around every fixture, and those inches decide what fits. Designers recommend more room where you can spare it.

Fixture

Code minimum

More comfortable

Toilet, center to side wall or vanity

15 in.

18 in.

Clear space in front of the toilet

21 in.

30 in.

Sink, center to side wall

15 in.

20 in.

Shower interior

30 x 30 in.

36 x 36 in.

The code minimums follow the International Residential Code. The comfortable column follows National Kitchen & Bath Association planning guidelines. Your city may use a different code edition, so confirm with your local building department.

Compact fixtures make these numbers easier to hit. Small single-sink vanities commonly come in 24, 30 and 36 inch widths. Compact freestanding tubs run under 54 inches long, against 60 inches for a standard alcove tub.

Showers have more range than most people expect. A width of 32 inches works in a very tight room. Fine Homebuilding recommends 36 inches as a practical minimum and 42 to 48 inches for comfort.

Here's how it adds up in a 5-by-8-foot bathroom, which is 40 square feet. A 30-inch-wide tub sits across one end of the 96-inch wall. The toilet takes its 30 inches. That leaves 36 inches for a vanity, which is the largest of the common compact sizes.

Small bathroom remodel ideas under $1,500

These are cosmetic upgrades. Nothing moves, no walls open up, and most of the work fits into a weekend or two.

1. Repaint in a light, moisture-resistant finish

Paint is the cheapest way to change how big the room feels. A bathroom paint job costs $70 to $250, according to Angi. Off-white, tan and white lead the color choices in the NKBA 2026 Bath Trends Report.

Paint the ceiling the same light color as the walls, because a contrast line makes it feel lower. Choose a satin or semi-gloss finish, since both handle moisture better than flat paint.

2. Hang one large mirror

A mirror that spans the vanity wall doubles the visual depth of the room. It also bounces light into corners a single fixture can't reach. One large mirror does more than two small ones, and a frameless edge keeps it from looking heavy.

3. Layer the lighting

A single ceiling light leaves shadows at the mirror and makes the room feel flat. Use three layers instead. Recessed, wet-rated lights on a dimmer handle general light. Sconces at face height on both sides of the mirror handle grooming.

An LED strip under the vanity or inside a niche adds depth at night. Lighting also ranked first among wellness features in the 2026 Houzz study, ahead of soaker tubs and radiant floors. Swapping a fixture is a DIY job, but new wiring needs an electrician.

4. Match the hardware and faucet

Mismatched finishes make a small room look busy. Replacing pulls, towel hooks and the faucet in one finish pulls it together. Hardware runs $3 to $200 per piece. The NKBA reports that matte, brushed and satin finishes are gaining on polished ones.

5. Raise the shower curtain to the ceiling

If glass isn't in the budget, hang an extra-long curtain close to the ceiling. The long vertical line makes the walls read as taller. Choose a light, plain fabric so it doesn't cut the room in half.

6. Use the wall above the toilet

This wall is wasted in most small bathrooms. A shallow cabinet or two shelves here adds storage without touching the floor. A closed cabinet hides clutter better than open shelves, which matters in a room this size.

7. Upgrade the exhaust fan

Small bathrooms trap moisture quickly, and moisture ruins new paint and grout. The Home Ventilating Institute recommends 1 CFM of fan capacity per square foot, with a 50 CFM minimum for bathrooms of 50 square feet or less.

The fan should vent outdoors, never into the attic. Replacing a fan in the same spot is simple. Running new ducting is a job for a pro.

8. Add a bidet seat

A bidet seat replaces the existing toilet seat, so it adds comfort without using any space. Almost half of renovating homeowners now add specialty toilet features such as bidet seats, per Houzz. Most models need an electrical outlet near the toilet.

9. Rehang the door to swing out

A 30-inch door that swings inward sweeps about five square feet of floor. In a 40-square-foot room, that's an eighth of the space. Reversing the hinges so the door opens outward gives that floor back for the cost of a handyman visit.

Small bathroom remodel ideas from $1,500 to $6,000

At this level you replace what's worn but keep the plumbing where it is. A 30-square-foot full bathroom typically costs $4,500 to $6,000 to remodel this way, per Angi.

10. Install a floating vanity

A wall-mounted vanity lets the floor run underneath, and visible floor is what makes a small room read as larger. A prefab vanity costs $100 to $2,600. Pick one with drawers, because drawers use the full depth of the cabinet and doors don't.

Wood-tone vanities are the most popular choice in the 2026 Houzz study, ahead of white and blue. The wall needs solid blocking to carry the weight, so this is a job for a pro.

11. Recess a medicine cabinet

A recessed medicine cabinet sits between the wall studs, so it adds storage without sticking out into the room. It also doubles as the mirror. Newer models include lighting, defoggers and outlets inside, which keeps chargers and hair tools off the counter.

12. Build a shower niche

A niche replaces the caddies and corner shelves that crowd a small shower. It's framed between the studs and tiled to match the wall, so it almost disappears. The best time to add one is during a retile, when the wall is already open.

13. Lay large-format tile or vinyl plank

Fewer grout lines make a floor look calmer and larger. The NKBA expects large-format tile to stay the top tile selection. Porcelain tile runs $0.50 to $15 per square foot, and vinyl costs $2 to $7.

Large tile needs a flat subfloor, so budget for prep work. Vinyl plank is waterproof and easier on the budget. Inside the shower, use a small mosaic on the floor, since the extra grout lines give more grip.

14. Switch to a compact toilet

A compact or round-front toilet projects less into the room than a standard elongated one. Those few inches can be the difference between meeting the 21-inch front clearance and missing it. A new toilet costs $225 to $3,000 depending on the model.

15. Replace the curtain with clear glass

A shower curtain or frosted door stops your eye halfway across the room. A clear, frameless glass panel lets you see all the way to the back wall. It's one of the biggest visual changes you can make without changing the layout.

16. Convert the tub to a shower

A tub-to-shower conversion costs about $3,000, according to Angi. You gain easier entry and more standing room in the same footprint. Before you commit, read the shower or tub section below, because the right answer depends on who uses the bathroom.

17. Fit a pocket or sliding door

A pocket door slides into the wall and removes the door swing completely. A surface-mounted sliding door does the same job without opening the wall. Either one helps most where the door currently hits a fixture or blocks the vanity.

18. Use a corner or console sink

In a half bath, a full vanity is often more cabinet than you need. A corner sink clears the walkway. A console sink on thin legs keeps the floor visible and can double as a towel bar. You give up storage, so pair it with a recessed cabinet.

19. Add one tile accent wall

Keep pattern to one surface and let the rest stay quiet. Just over a third of renovating homeowners added an accent wall, per Houzz. Herringbone, checkerboard and geometric layouts lead, and fluted or ribbed tile adds texture without adding color.

The wall behind the vanity or the back wall of the shower works best. Both are where your eye lands first.

20. Add a heated floor or towel warmer

Small rooms make comfort upgrades more affordable, because there's less area to cover. Radiant floor heat goes under the tile, so plan it with a new floor. A wall-mounted towel warmer takes no floor space. Both need an electrician.

21. Plan for grab bars and a slip-resistant floor

Grab bars and non-slip flooring are the most popular aging-in-place features in the 2026 Houzz study. Even if you don't want bars now, add solid wood blocking behind the tile. It lets you mount them later without opening the wall.

Ask for floor tile rated for wet areas. Lever handles are another easy addition, since they work with wet or full hands.

Small bathroom remodel ideas from $6,000 to $15,000

This is a full remodel, with the room taken down to the studs. It's where new showers and new layouts become possible. A new shower costs $400 to $8,500 and a new tub $2,000 to $9,400, according to Angi. Plumbing work adds $1,000 to $2,000.

Hold back 10% to 15% of the budget as a contingency. Older bathrooms often hide water damage, and repairs run $3.75 to $7 per square foot, per NerdWallet.

22. Build a curbless walk-in shower

A curbless shower has no step at the entry. The bathroom floor slopes gently to the drain, so the tile runs through as one continuous surface. Most renovating homeowners now choose a low-curb or curbless shower, per Houzz.

It costs more than a standard shower because the subfloor has to be reworked to create the slope. A fixed glass panel keeps spray off the rest of the room.

23. Turn the room into a wet room

In a wet room, the entire bathroom is waterproofed and the shower is open to the rest of the space. Nothing is boxed off, so every square foot stays usable. Wet rooms now appear in 18% of bathroom renovations, up from 13% a couple of years ago, per Houzz.

Accessibility is the main reason homeowners choose one, followed by easier cleaning. Waterproofing quality is everything here, so hire a contractor who has built them before.

24. Fit a neo-angle shower

A neo-angle shower sits in a corner with the front corner clipped off. That clipped corner gives back floor space right where you walk. It suits small square bathrooms, such as 6 by 6 feet, where a rectangular shower would block the door or the toilet.

25. Choose a compact soaking tub

You don't have to give up a bath to save space. Compact freestanding tubs run under 54 inches long, and some are deeper than a standard tub. You sit more upright, but you still get a full soak in less floor length.

26. Install a wall-hung toilet

A wall-hung toilet hides its tank inside the wall. The bowl floats above the floor, which makes the room look bigger and far easier to clean. The wall has to be opened and reinforced for the carrier frame, which is why this belongs in a full remodel.

27. Rework the fixture layout

Sometimes the floor plan is the problem. The door hits the toilet, or the vanity blocks the shower. Moving fixtures can fix that, but a new floor plan adds about $5,000 for plumbing and electrical changes, per NerdWallet.

Try the cheaper fixes first. Keeping the sink, toilet and shower along one wall keeps pipe runs short. If you do move things, expect to need permits, which cost $100 to $1,000.

Shower or tub in a small bathroom?

Most homeowners are choosing the shower. Enlarging the shower was the fastest-growing major change in the 2026 Houzz study, and the NKBA 2026 Bath Trends Report found larger showers preferred over bathtubs.

That doesn't make a shower right for every home. A walk-in shower suits a household of adults, or a home that already has a tub in another bathroom. It's also the better choice if stepping over a tub wall is getting harder.

Keep a tub if this is the only bathroom in the house or you bathe young children. A tub-shower combo is the most space-efficient way to have both. In a 5-foot-wide room, a standard 60-inch alcove tub fits wall to wall with a clear glass screen on top.

If you want a bath but can't spare 60 inches, a compact soaking tub is the middle ground. If accessibility matters most, go curbless.

Modern small bathroom design ideas for 2026

Not every 2026 trend suits a small room, but several of the biggest ones do.

The overall direction is warm and simple. Transitional style leads both the NKBA and Houzz research, which means clean lines without a stark, ultra-modern feel. Light neutrals form the base, with sage and olive green as the favored accents. In a small bathroom, that translates to pale walls and one green element, such as the vanity or a band of tile.

Materials are getting warmer too. Wood-faced vanities are gaining on painted ones, according to the NKBA. In a room full of tile, glass and porcelain, one wood surface keeps it from feeling cold. Matte, brushed and satin metal finishes are gaining on polished ones.

Tile is getting larger and more textured. Large-format tile stays on top because homeowners want fewer grout lines. Fluted and ribbed tile is the texture of the moment. Both work in small rooms as long as the pattern stays on one surface.

Two popular trends are worth skipping. Double sinks are up 17% and vanities are getting larger, per Houzz. Both take floor space a small bathroom doesn't have. A single sink with more counter and drawer space serves most households better.

The right ideas depend on which small bathroom you have. Typical sizes and 2026 remodel costs below are from Angi.

A half bath has no shower steam, so wallpaper and darker colors hold up better there than in a full bath. It's the one small room where a bold choice is low risk.

A small full bathroom benefits most from glass and wall-mounted fixtures. A small primary bathroom gets used every day, so spend on the shower and on drawer storage first.

A windowless bathroom needs the most help with light. Use all three lighting layers, a large mirror and pale walls, and make sure the fan is sized for the room.

What the photos don't show

The parts you can't see decide how long a remodel lasts. They matter even more in a small bathroom, where moisture has less room to escape.

Start with waterproofing. Tile and grout are not waterproof on their own. A membrane behind the tile is what keeps water out of the wall, and a failed one shows up months later as stains or loose tile.

Next, check on permits. Moving plumbing, adding circuits or changing walls usually requires one, while paint and hardware usually don't. Rules vary by city, so call your local building department before work starts.

How long does a small bathroom remodel take?

A small bathroom remodel with a new shower or vanity typically takes two to four weeks. A full gut can run four to eight weeks or more. Paint and hardware alone can be done in a weekend.

The work follows the same order every time. Demolition comes first, then plumbing and electrical rough-in, which gets inspected. Waterproofing and tile follow. Fixtures, glass and lighting go in last, before a final inspection.

Most delays come from materials, not labor. Special-order tile and custom glass can take weeks to arrive. Order everything before demolition begins so the room isn't sitting empty.

DIY or hire a pro?

Do the surface work yourself if you want to save, and hire licensed trades for anything behind the wall. Labor makes up 40% to 60% of a small bathroom remodel, so the DIY savings are real.

Painting, hardware, mirrors and shelves are safe to take on with basic tools. A vanity swap in the same location is manageable if the plumbing lines up. Floor tile is possible for a patient DIYer with a flat subfloor.

Leave the rest to professionals. Shower waterproofing mistakes cause hidden leaks. Moving plumbing and adding circuits are licensed work in most places and need permits. Frameless glass is heavy, custom-measured and easy to break.

When you hire a contractor, check these before you sign:

  • Verify the license with your state licensing board.

  • Ask for proof of liability insurance.

  • Get at least three written quotes for the same scope.

  • Ask to see finished small bathrooms, not just large ones.

  • Confirm who pulls the permits.

  • Get the payment schedule and warranty in writing.

Is a small bathroom remodel worth it?

Modest bathroom remodels return far more of their cost than luxury ones, and that works in favor of small bathrooms.

In the 2025 Cost vs. Value Report, a midrange bath remodel averaged $26,138 and recouped 80% of its cost at resale. An upscale remodel averaged $81,612 and recouped just 42%. A universal design remodel, built around accessibility, recouped 61%.

Those projects are larger than a typical small bathroom, which averages $6,500. The pattern still holds: the more restrained the remodel, the more of it you get back. Angi puts the average return on a bathroom remodel at 55% to 60%.

Mistakes that make a small bathroom feel smaller

Most small-bathroom regrets come from adding too much. A common one is an oversized vanity, bought before anyone checked the clearances. Another is using several tile patterns at once, which makes the room feel busy and tight.

Lighting and glass cause the next round of problems. A single ceiling light leaves shadows at the mirror. Frosted glass or a dark shower curtain cuts the room in half.

The expensive mistakes are the hidden ones. Skipping the fan upgrade lets moisture ruin new paint and grout. Moving plumbing without a clear reason is the fastest way to add $5,000 to the budget.

Frequently asked questions

How much does it cost to remodel a small bathroom?

A small bathroom remodel averages $6,500 in 2026, with most projects between $1,500 and $15,000, according to Angi. A half bath runs $2,250 to $3,000, and a small full bath runs $4,500 to $6,000.

What is the cheapest way to remodel a small bathroom?

Keep every fixture where it is and change the surfaces. Paint, a larger mirror, new lighting and matching hardware can come in under $1,500. Layout changes are what push costs up.

How do you make a small bathroom look bigger?

Use one large mirror, clear glass, light walls and large-format tile. Run the same flooring into the shower if you can. Mount the vanity on the wall so the floor stays visible.

What color looks best in a small bathroom?

White, off-white and warm neutrals reflect the most light. Add one accent, such as sage or olive green, on the vanity or a single wall. Dark colors work best in powder rooms with strong lighting.

What is the best bathroom design for small spaces?

Line the sink, toilet and shower along one wall and keep the door from swinging into them. In a 5x8 room, the tub or shower sits across the far end. That layout keeps plumbing costs low and the walkway clear.

How long does a small bathroom remodel take?

A remodel with a new shower or vanity typically takes two to four weeks. A full gut can run four to eight weeks. Paint and hardware alone take a weekend.

What are the small bathroom trends for 2026?

Bigger showers, curbless entries, large-format tile, wood-tone vanities and matte finishes lead this year. Light neutrals with green accents are the top color direction. Bidet seats are also becoming common.

Can you fit a bathtub in a tiny bathroom?

Yes, if one wall is at least 5 feet long. A standard alcove tub is 60 inches, and compact freestanding tubs run under 54 inches. A tub-shower combo is the most space-efficient choice.

How do you decorate a small bathroom with no window?

Start with light. Use bright ambient lighting, sconces at the mirror and a large mirror to spread it around. Choose pale wall colors and make sure the exhaust fan is sized for the room.

Do I need a permit to remodel a small bathroom?

Usually yes if you move plumbing, add electrical circuits or change walls. Cosmetic work such as paint and hardware usually doesn't need one. Rules vary, so check with your local building department.
